title: Use Map Robot Selection “Go to” to reposition an AGV to a selected square
summary: Use the RMS / fleet status UI map’s Robot Selection “Go to” workflow to send an AGV that is not currently in a task to a selected destination square. The source presents this as a quick recovery method for a stalled/blocked situation (example: a tipper goes down and an AGV will not leave; after the tote is removed, the AGV can pick up a new task).
when_to_use: When an AGV is not in a task and you need to recover quickly by sending it to a chosen map square using Robot Selection “Go to” (example use case described: a tipper goes down and an AGV will not leave; after the tote is removed, the AGV can resume by picking up a new task).

steps.title: Open the RMS map view that supports selecting operational objects
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI, open the map view that allows selecting operational objects (AGVs/cells). Avoid clicking only on the map background.
steps.purpose: Ensure the map is in an object-select mode so selecting an AGV triggers the Robot Selection workflow (not a generic map click).
steps.expected_result: You can select operational objects on the map (AGV/cell selection is recognized by the UI).
steps.healthy_condition: Selecting an AGV object is possible; generic map clicking does not perform the Robot Selection action.
steps.failure_condition: If you click on the map background (not an operational object), no Robot Selection action occurs.

actions.label: Verify object-select behavior
actions.exact_action: Select operational objects on the map (not just click on the map background).

steps.title: Select the specific AGV object on the map
steps.instruction: On the RMS map, select the specific AGV object (do not select a generic map area).
steps.purpose: Target the correct AGV for the Robot Selection “Go to” command.
steps.expected_result: The selected AGV is identified by the UI as the target for Robot Selection.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV object selection is active (the UI is ready to show Robot Selection options for that AGV).
steps.failure_condition: No AGV is selected (or selection is not recognized), so Robot Selection options cannot be applied to the intended AGV.

actions.label: Select AGV object
actions.exact_action: Select an AGV.

steps.title: Select the Robot Selection “Go to” function for the selected AGV
steps.instruction: After selecting the AGV on the RMS map, choose the Robot Selection “Go to” function for that AGV.
steps.purpose: Choose the command that repositions an AGV that is not currently in a task.
steps.expected_result: The UI enters the “Go to” flow for the selected AGV (ready to choose a destination square).
steps.healthy_condition: “Go to” is selected for the AGV and the next action is selecting a destination square.
steps.failure_condition: “Go to” is not available/does not activate for the selected AGV, or the UI does not proceed to destination square selection.

actions.label: Choose Go to
actions.exact_action: Select Go to.

steps.title: Select the destination square on the map
steps.instruction: In the “Go to” flow, select the destination square on the RMS map where you want the AGV to go.
steps.purpose: Define where the AGV should be repositioned.
steps.expected_result: A destination square is selected as the target for the AGV “Go to” command.
steps.healthy_condition: The chosen square is accepted by the UI and the flow proceeds to confirmation.
steps.failure_condition: No destination square can be selected/accepted, or the UI does not proceed to the Confirm step.

actions.label: Select destination square
actions.exact_action: Select which square you want the AGV to go to.

steps.title: Select “Confirm” to send the AGV to the selected square
steps.instruction: Select “Confirm” to send the selected AGV to the selected destination square.
steps.purpose: Transmit the reposition command to the system.
steps.expected_result: The “Go to” command is confirmed and issued for the selected AGV to the selected square.
steps.healthy_condition: After confirmation, the AGV is no longer treated as “not in a task” and can resume work after the described recovery condition is cleared.
steps.failure_condition: The map action does not take effect (e.g., the AGV does not move / does not resume tasking after the recovery condition described).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the map action does not take effect (e.g., selecting the map background causes no action, or the AGV does not move / does not resume tasking after the recovery condition described).
If the AGV remains unable to leave the area despite using “Go to,” escalate for deeper troubleshooting of the underlying blockage.

actions.label: Confirm Go to
actions.exact_action: Select Confirm.

steps.title: Verify AGV resumes tasking after the described recovery condition (e.g., tote removed)
steps.instruction: After issuing “Go to” and clearing the described blockage condition (example: tote removed), observe that the AGV resumes by picking up a new task.
steps.purpose: Confirm the recovery outcome: the AGV can pick up a new task once the blocking tote is removed.
steps.expected_result: The AGV picks up a new task after its tote has been removed (as described in the recovery example).
steps.healthy_condition: AGV tasking resumes after the tote removal; the AGV is no longer stuck in the described “not leaving” situation.
steps.failure_condition: AGV remains unable to leave the area and does not resume tasking after the recovery condition described.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the AGV remains unable to leave the area despite using “Go to,” escalate for deeper troubleshooting of the underlying blockage (example ties recovery to tipper-down and tote removal).

actions.label: Observe task resumption
actions.exact_action: Observe that the AGV will pickup a new task once it's tote has been removed.

title: Check Overall System AGV Status popup for AGVs with destination errors
summary: Use the live RMS / fleet status UI popup titled “Overall System AGV Status” to identify which AGVs currently have errors and review their Destination and Errors details. The popup shows a top section for all AGVs and a bottom section filtered to only AGVs with errors.
when_to_use: When you need to quickly determine which AGVs have active errors related to destination/error conditions and view their Destination and Errors details in the RMS fleet status UI.

steps.title: Open the RMS “Overall System AGV Status” popup
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), navigate to the popup/screen titled “Overall System AGV Status”.
steps.purpose: Get to the correct RMS popup that contains the AGV ID, Status, Destination, and Errors fields and the error-filtered bottom section.
steps.expected_result: The “Overall System AGV Status” popup is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The popup title “Overall System AGV Status” is visible and the popup is rendered with both top and bottom sections.
steps.failure_condition: The popup does not display the “Overall System AGV Status” title or does not render the expected popup content.

actions.label: Verify popup title
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI and navigate to the popup/screen titled “Overall System AGV Status”.

steps.title: Confirm top section fields for all AGVs (ID, Status, Destination, Errors)
steps.instruction: In the “Overall System AGV Status” popup, check the top section table/list to confirm it includes fields/columns for ID, Status, Destination, and Errors.
steps.purpose: Ensure the popup is showing the required columns/fields so you can interpret which AGVs have errors.
steps.expected_result: The top section displays the fields/columns “ID”, “Status”, “Destination”, and “Errors”.
steps.healthy_condition: The top section shows a detailed table/list for all AGVs with visible column headers/fields: ID, Status, Destination, Errors.
steps.failure_condition: The popup top section is missing one or more expected fields/columns (ID/Status/Destination/Errors).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the popup fails to display the expected fields (ID/Status/Destination/Errors).

actions.label: Check column headers
actions.exact_action: In the top section, confirm the popup shows a detailed table/list for all AGVs with columns/fields for ID, Status, Destination, and Errors.

steps.title: Confirm bottom section is filtered to AGVs with errors
steps.instruction: In the “Overall System AGV Status” popup, check the bottom section to confirm it lists only AGVs with errors and includes additional error/destination detail for those AGVs.
steps.purpose: Verify the error-only filtering behavior so you can trust the bottom list for error AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The bottom section lists only AGVs with errors (error cases) and shows additional detail for those error AGVs.
steps.healthy_condition: The bottom section contains only error AGVs and additional detail is present for those error cases.
steps.failure_condition: The bottom section is empty when the top section indicates any AGV has a non-empty Errors value, or the bottom section does not behave as an error-only list.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the bottom section is empty while the top section indicates any AGV has a non-empty Errors value.
Escalate if the bottom section does not behave as described (should show only AGVs with errors).

actions.label: Verify error-only filtering
actions.exact_action: In the bottom section, confirm only AGVs with errors appear and that additional detail is shown for those error AGVs.

steps.title: Record AGV IDs and their Destination/Errors from the error-only bottom section
steps.instruction: For each AGV listed in the bottom (error-only) section, record/verify the AGV ID and the associated Destination and Errors details displayed in the popup.
steps.purpose: Capture the specific AGVs currently showing errors and the associated Destination and Errors details for follow-up troubleshooting/escalation.
steps.expected_result: You have a list of AGV IDs from the bottom section along with their displayed Destination and Errors values.
steps.healthy_condition: Each bottom-section row corresponds to an error case and includes the AGV ID plus Destination and Errors details.
steps.failure_condition: Bottom-section rows are missing AGV ID or do not show Destination/Errors details needed to identify the error case.

actions.label: Capture error AGV details
actions.exact_action: For each AGV shown in the bottom (error-only) section, record/verify the AGV ID and the associated Destination and Errors details displayed in the popup.

steps.title: Escalate if popup fields are missing or error-only list behavior is inconsistent
steps.instruction: If the popup does not show the expected “Overall System AGV Status” title/fields (ID, Status, Destination, Errors) or if the bottom section does not correctly show only AGVs with errors, stop and escalate.
steps.purpose: Ensure you stop and escalate when the UI does not match the expected behavior, preventing incorrect conclusions.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated when UI evidence is inconsistent with expected fields or filtering behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: No escalation is required because the popup title/fields are present and the bottom section correctly reflects error-only AGVs.
steps.failure_condition: UI evidence is inconsistent (missing fields or incorrect bottom-section filtering).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the popup does not show the expected “Overall System AGV Status” title/fields (ID, Status, Destination, Errors).
Escalate if the bottom section does not behave as described (should show only AGVs with errors).

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the bottom section is empty while the top section indicates any AGV has a non-empty Errors value, or if the popup fails to display the expected fields (ID/Status/Destination/Errors).

title: Verify Tote Exchange Settings Thresholds and Method on AVEVA HMI
summary: On the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page, verify the configured cube/count thresholds for Pickup, Priority, and Close, plus weight-related parameters (Maximum Weight, Weight Threshold) and the selected Method (Count, Cube, Cube and Count) so tote exchange behavior uses the correct evaluation logic.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm the active tote exchange configuration on the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page—specifically the queue/pickup/priority/close thresholds for both Cube and Count, the weight-related parameters (Maximum Weight, Weight Threshold), and the selected evaluation Method (Count/Cube/Cube and Count).

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page
steps.instruction: Using the AVEVA HMI interface, open the Tote Exchange Settings screen (Tote Exchange Settings interface).
steps.purpose: Get to the live Tote Exchange Settings interface so you can verify the configured thresholds and Method.
steps.expected_result: The AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page is displayed with fields for Cube Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close, Count Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close, Maximum Weight, Weight Threshold, and a Method field.
steps.healthy_condition: The Tote Exchange Settings page loads and shows the threshold and Method fields (not blank/undefined).
steps.failure_condition: The Tote Exchange Settings page cannot be opened, or required fields are missing/blank/undefined.

actions.label: Open Tote Exchange Settings
actions.exact_action: Open the AVEVA HMI screen for Tote Exchange Settings (Tote Exchange Settings interface).

steps.title: Verify Cube thresholds for Pickup, Priority, and Close
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page, locate and review the Cube threshold fields: Cube Threshold Pickup, Cube Threshold Priority, and Cube Threshold Close.
steps.purpose: Confirm the Cube-based queue/pickup/priority/close thresholds are configured as expected.
steps.expected_result: Cube Threshold Pickup, Cube Threshold Priority, and Cube Threshold Close are populated with valid values (not blank/invalid).
steps.healthy_condition: All three Cube threshold fields show populated values.
steps.failure_condition: Any Cube threshold field is blank/invalid.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any required threshold fields are blank/invalid.

actions.label: Check Cube Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close
actions.exact_action: Locate the threshold fields for Cube: Cube Threshold Pickup, Cube Threshold Priority, and Cube Threshold Close.

steps.title: Verify Count thresholds for Pickup, Priority, and Close
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page, locate and review the Count threshold fields: Count Threshold Pickup, Count Threshold Priority, and Count Threshold Close.
steps.purpose: Confirm the Count-based queue/pickup/priority/close thresholds are configured as expected.
steps.expected_result: Count Threshold Pickup, Count Threshold Priority, and Count Threshold Close are populated with valid values (not blank/invalid).
steps.healthy_condition: All three Count threshold fields show populated values.
steps.failure_condition: Any Count threshold field is blank/invalid.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any required threshold fields are blank/invalid.

actions.label: Check Count Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close
actions.exact_action: Locate the threshold fields for Count: Count Threshold Pickup, Count Threshold Priority, and Count Threshold Close.

steps.title: Verify weight-related parameters (Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold)
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page, locate and review the weight-related fields: Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold.
steps.purpose: Confirm the weight-related parameters used in tote exchange evaluation are configured.
steps.expected_result: Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold are populated with valid values (not blank/invalid).
steps.healthy_condition: Both weight fields show populated values.
steps.failure_condition: Either Maximum Weight or Weight Threshold is blank/invalid.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any required threshold/weight fields are blank/invalid.

actions.label: Check Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold
actions.exact_action: Locate weight-related fields: Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold.

steps.title: Verify the Tote Exchange Settings Method selection
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI Tote Exchange Settings page, locate the Method field and confirm it is set to one of the available options: Count, Cube, or Cube and Count.
steps.purpose: Confirm the evaluation logic method is set to one of the supported options.
steps.expected_result: Method is set to Count, Cube, or Cube and Count (not blank/undefined).
steps.healthy_condition: Method shows one of the supported options: Count, Cube, or Cube and Count.
steps.failure_condition: Method is blank/undefined or not one of the expected options.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Method is not one of the expected options (Count/Cube/Cube and Count) or if any required threshold fields are blank/invalid.

actions.label: Check Method option
actions.exact_action: Locate the Method field and confirm it is set to one of the available options: Count, Cube, or Cube and Count.

steps.title: Confirm configured values match expected tote exchange configuration
steps.instruction: Compare the displayed Cube Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close, Count Threshold Pickup/Priority/Close, Maximum Weight/Weight Threshold, and Method selection against the expected tote exchange configuration for the active project/UAT-finalized settings. If values are consistent, stop; otherwise escalate for configuration correction.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the displayed thresholds/weight parameters and Method align with the expected tote exchange configuration for the active project/UAT-finalized settings.
steps.expected_result: All displayed threshold/weight fields and the Method selection match the expected configuration for the active project/UAT-finalized settings.
steps.healthy_condition: Cube and Count thresholds are populated and Method is set to Count, Cube, or Cube and Count; weight fields are populated.
steps.failure_condition: Any configured thresholds/weight parameters do not align with the expected tote exchange configuration for the active project/UAT-finalized settings.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the configured thresholds/weight parameters do not align with the expected tote exchange configuration for the active project/UAT-finalized settings.

actions.label: Compare to expected configuration
actions.exact_action: Observe whether the configured values match what the site/project expects for the tote exchange thresholds (queue/pickup/priority/close thresholds and the selected evaluation method). Stop if values are consistent; otherwise escalate for configuration correction.

title: Cancel Manual Bag Out (cancel exchange tasks not in process)
summary: When a manual bag out is initiated, cancel the bag out for exchange tasks that are not already in process, while ensuring any exchange already in process still completes.
when_to_use: Use when a manual bag out has been initiated and you need to cancel the bag out effect for exchange tasks that are not already in process, while allowing in-process exchanges to finish.

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI Overall System bag out view
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI (Overall System view), navigate to the bag out controls area where the “cancel bag out” option is available.
steps.purpose: Access the live bag out controls that include the “cancel bag out” option.
steps.expected_result: The AVEVA HMI bag out controls are visible, including the “cancel bag out” option.
steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly see the bag out control panel with the “cancel bag out” option available for selection.
steps.failure_condition: The “cancel bag out” option is not visible/accessible, or you cannot locate the bag out control panel.

actions.label: Open bag out controls
actions.exact_action: Open the AVEVA HMI overall system view that contains the bag out controls and the cancel bag out option.

steps.title: Confirm the bag out is manual (not system bag out)
steps.instruction: In the AVEVA HMI bag out controls, confirm the current bag out action is a manual bag out (not a system bag out).
steps.purpose: Ensure the “cancel bag out” behavior applies to the correct bag out type.
steps.expected_result: You can identify that the active bag out is manual, so “cancel bag out” applies to exchange tasks not in process.
steps.healthy_condition: Manual bag out context/indicator is clearly selected/active in the AVEVA HMI bag out controls.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot clearly determine whether the active bag out is manual vs system bag out.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly identify which exchanges are “in process,” stop and escalate for support to avoid incorrect conclusions.

actions.label: Check manual vs system bag out
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the current action is a manual bag out (not a system bag out) so the cancel bag out capability applies.

steps.title: Select “cancel bag out”
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI bag out controls, click/select “cancel bag out”.
steps.purpose: Trigger cancellation so exchange tasks not in process are canceled.
steps.expected_result: The “cancel bag out” action is executed from the AVEVA HMI controls.
steps.healthy_condition: The “cancel bag out” control is successfully selected (no immediate UI error/blocked action).
steps.failure_condition: The “cancel bag out” action cannot be executed (control not responsive/blocked) or does not take effect.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if cancel bag out fails to cancel exchanges that are not in process.

actions.label: Cancel bag out
actions.exact_action: Select/click “cancel bag out” (cancel bag out).

steps.title: Verify cancellation scope: exchanges not in process are canceled
steps.instruction: After clicking “cancel bag out,” verify that exchange tasks/chests that are NOT in process are canceled in the AVEVA HMI bag out/exchange status area.
steps.purpose: Confirm the cancel bag out behavior targets only exchange tasks/chests that are not already in process.
steps.expected_result: Exchange tasks/chests that were not in process are canceled.
steps.healthy_condition: You observe exchange tasks/chests transitioning to a canceled state for those that were not in process.
steps.failure_condition: Cancel bag out does not cancel exchange tasks/chests that were not in process.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if cancel bag out fails to cancel exchanges that are not in process.

actions.label: Check exchange status scope
actions.exact_action: Verify cancellation scope: exchange tasks/chests that are NOT in process should be canceled.

steps.title: Verify in-process exchanges still complete
steps.instruction: After clicking “cancel bag out,” verify that any exchange task that is already in process continues and completes.
steps.purpose: Ensure cancel bag out does not interrupt exchanges that are already in process.
steps.expected_result: Exchange tasks already in process continue and reach completion after cancel bag out.
steps.healthy_condition: You observe in-process exchange activity continuing to completion (not being canceled).
steps.failure_condition: Cancel bag out cancels exchanges that are already in process.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if cancel bag out cancels exchanges that are already in process.

actions.label: Check in-process completion
actions.exact_action: Verify in-process exchanges still complete: any exchange task that is already in process should still finish.

title: Use AVEVA Overall System Bag Out Control to perform System Bag Out / Pre Bag Out / Bag Out by Sorter Leg
summary: Use the AVEVA HMI “Overall System Bag Out Control” to run bag-out actions with the documented scope behavior: “System Bag Out” closes all destinations and exchanges all totes with parcels; “Bag out by leg of the sorter” limits the exchange to a selected sorter leg; “Pre bag out” exchanges the lowest 25% of destinations per sorter leg.
when_to_use: When you need to execute the documented overall bag-out actions (System Bag Out, Bag out by leg of the sorter, or Pre bag out) and verify that the resulting scope matches the selected mode (destinations closed and tote exchanges).

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI “Overall System Bag Out Control” view
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI (Overall System), navigate to the “Overall System Bag Out Control” screen/view that provides bag-out options.
steps.purpose: Access the controls that define and initiate the overall bag-out modes.
steps.expected_result: The AVEVA “Overall System Bag Out Control” view is open and shows bag-out options including “System Bag Out” and the option to bag out by leg of the sorter; the view also supports “Pre bag out.”
steps.healthy_condition: The bag-out options are visible on the AVEVA Overall System Bag Out Control view (System Bag Out, bag out by leg of the sorter, and Pre bag out).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the “Overall System Bag Out Control” view or the bag-out options are not available/visible.

actions.label: Navigate to Overall System Bag Out Control
actions.exact_action: Open the site HMI screen that provides “Overall System Bag Out Control” (AVEVA HMI / Overall System).

steps.title: Select the desired bag-out mode (System Bag Out vs Bag out by leg of the sorter)
steps.instruction: In the AVEVA “Overall System Bag Out Control” view, select either “System Bag Out” (overall) or “Bag out by leg of the sorter” (leg-specific).
steps.purpose: Choose the scope behavior that will be applied when you initiate bag-out.
steps.expected_result: The selected mode is set so that the bag-out scope will follow the documented behavior for that mode.
steps.healthy_condition: The UI selection reflects either overall “System Bag Out” or “Bag out by leg of the sorter.”
steps.failure_condition: The selected mode cannot be set/confirmed, or the UI does not present the expected mode options.

actions.label: Select bag-out mode
actions.exact_action: Select the desired bag-out mode: “System Bag Out” (overall) or “Bag out by leg of the sorter” (leg-specific).

steps.title: If needed, enable “Pre bag out” and set its scope to the lowest 25% per sorter leg
steps.instruction: If you are performing “Pre bag out,” set/choose the “Pre bag out” option so it exchanges the lowest 25% of destinations per leg of the sorter.
steps.purpose: Run the pre-bag-out scope behavior defined for the lowest 25% of destinations per sorter leg.
steps.expected_result: The “Pre bag out” option is selected such that the exchange scope will be limited to the lowest 25% of destinations per sorter leg.
steps.healthy_condition: The AVEVA “Pre bag out” option is selected and corresponds to the documented lowest-25%-per-leg behavior.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot select “Pre bag out,” or the UI does not reflect the lowest-25%-per-leg scope behavior.

actions.label: Select Pre bag out
actions.exact_action: If using “Pre bag out,” set/choose the “Pre bag out” option so it exchanges the lowest 25% of destinations per leg of the sorter.

steps.title: Initiate bag-out and verify the resulting scope matches the selected mode
steps.instruction: Initiate the bag-out action from the AVEVA “Overall System Bag Out Control” view, then observe that the bag-out scope matches the selected mode.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the bag-out action produced the documented scope behavior for the selected mode.
steps.expected_result: Observed scope matches the selected mode: (1) System Bag Out closes all destinations and exchanges all totes with parcels in them; (2) Bag out by leg applies to the chosen sorter leg; (3) Pre bag out exchanges the lowest 25% of destinations per leg.
steps.healthy_condition: The AVEVA bag-out scope/summary reflects the correct destination-closure and tote-exchange scope for the selected mode.
steps.failure_condition: The observed scope does not match the selected mode (e.g., destinations are not closed for System Bag Out, or tote exchange scope does not align with “all totes with parcels” / “lowest 25% per leg”).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the procedure if the observed scope does not match the selected mode (e.g., destinations are not closed for System Bag Out, or tote exchange scope does not align with “all totes with parcels” / “lowest 25% per leg”).

actions.label: Initiate bag-out
actions.exact_action: After initiating, observe that the bag-out scope matches the selected mode.

title: Verify System Bag Out Behavior (close destinations + exchange totes with parcels)
summary: Verify that a system bag out action closes all destinations and exchanges totes/chutes that contain parcels, and that the bag out scope matches the documented behavior (system-wide vs bag out by leg of the sorter).
when_to_use: Use to live-verify that the system bag out behavior closes destinations and exchanges parcel-containing totes/chutes, and to confirm whether the operator-selected bag out scope is system-wide or by leg of the sorter.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a generic response to any site stoppage without bag-out evidence; it is specifically for validating bag out behavior (destination closure + parcel-containing tote/chute exchange).

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI overall system view that contains the bag out controls
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI, navigate to the Overall System System Detail / overall system overview area that includes the Bag Out control.
steps.purpose: Get to the live AVEVA HMI screen where the system bag out action can be initiated and where destination status can be observed.
steps.expected_result: The AVEVA HMI overall system view is open and shows the Bag Out control area (bag out is available from the overall system overview).
steps.healthy_condition: Bag Out control is visible on the overall system overview (operator can initiate bag out from this view).
steps.failure_condition: Bag Out control is not visible on the overall system overview, or the operator cannot reach the bag out control area from the overall system view.

actions.label: Navigate to Overall System overview with Bag Out
actions.exact_action: Open the AVEVA HMI overall system view that contains the bag out controls.

steps.title: Initiate/observe the system bag out action (overall system bag out)
steps.instruction: From the AVEVA HMI bag out control area on the overall system view, initiate the system bag out action and observe the resulting behavior.
steps.purpose: Trigger the bag out behavior that should close all destinations and exchange parcel-containing totes/chutes.
steps.expected_result: After initiating system bag out, the system performs the documented behavior: destinations close and totes/chutes with parcels are exchanged.
steps.healthy_condition: System bag out completes with destinations closing and parcel-containing totes/chutes exchanging as part of bag out.
steps.failure_condition: Destinations do not close, or parcel-containing totes/chutes do not show exchange behavior consistent with bag out.

actions.label: Run system bag out
actions.exact_action: Initiate/observe the system bag out action (overall system bag out).

steps.title: Observe destination status after bag out (destinations should be closed)
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI overall system view, observe the destinations status after the system bag out action completes.
steps.purpose: Confirm the destination-closure portion of the system bag out behavior.
steps.expected_result: All destinations are closed as part of the system bag out behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: Destination indicators show a closed state after bag out.
steps.failure_condition: One or more destinations remain open/active after bag out.
stop_or_escalate_if: If destinations do not close, escalate.

actions.label: Check destination closed/active indicators
actions.exact_action: Observe the destinations status after bag out: destinations should be closed as part of the system bag out behavior.

steps.title: Observe tote/chute exchange behavior for parcel-containing items
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI overall system view, observe tote/chute exchange behavior after system bag out, focusing on totes/chutes that contain parcels.
steps.purpose: Confirm the exchange portion of the system bag out behavior for totes/chutes that contain parcels.
steps.expected_result: Parcel-containing totes/chutes are exchanged as part of bag out.
steps.healthy_condition: Parcel-containing totes/chutes show exchange state changes consistent with bag out.
steps.failure_condition: Parcel-containing totes/chutes do not show exchange behavior consistent with bag out.
stop_or_escalate_if: If parcel-containing totes/chutes do not show exchange behavior consistent with bag out, escalate.

actions.label: Check tote/chute exchange state changes
actions.exact_action: Observe tote/chute exchange behavior: parcel-containing totes/chutes should be exchanged as described (“exchange … with parcels in them”).

steps.title: Confirm bag out scope: system-wide vs bag out by leg of the sorter
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI bag out control area, confirm whether the bag out scope is set to full system bag out or “bag out by leg of the sorter.”

steps.healthy_condition: You can see the manual bag out popup/controls with the “cancel bag out” option available for selection.

title: Diagnose AGV exchange/backfill gap when an AGV moves out without a replacement
summary: Diagnose why a front AGV moved out without a replacement/backfill by checking (1) whether the trailing AGV had a fault (including the case where it was reported ready for a new task and faulted at the same time) and (2) whether chute closure/fullness and exchange timing targets indicate exchanges were not completed before chute closure.
when_to_use: Use when you observe or are told that an AGV moved out without another AGV backfilling/replacing it during an exchange, and you need live evidence to confirm whether the trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing and/or chute fullness/closure and exchange timing targets contributed.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for physical safety actions (e.g., E-stop/LOTO).

steps.title: Open RMS / fleet status UI and identify the AGV pair for the exchange event
steps.instruction: Using the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), locate the AGV pair involved in the exchange event: the AGV that moved out (front) and the AGV that should have backfilled (trailing).
steps.purpose: Establish which front AGV moved out and which trailing AGV should have backfilled so you can check the trailing AGV’s fault/ready+fault timing.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the specific trailing AGV associated with the exchange event time window (so you can check whether it faulted when the front AGV moved out).
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS view clearly shows the relevant AGVs and their status/error context for the exchange event you are investigating.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine which trailing AGV corresponds to the exchange event, or RMS does not provide enough context to identify the correct AGV pair/time window.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot identify the correct AGV pair/time window in RMS, proceed to WCS/Helix DB (SSMS) (wcs_sql) to find the relevant AGV records for the time window.

actions.label: Locate AGV pair in RMS
actions.exact_action: Open RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) and locate the AGV pair involved in the exchange event (the AGV that moved out and the AGV that should have backfilled).

steps.title: Check trailing AGV status for fault at the time the front AGV moved out
steps.instruction: In RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), check the trailing (behind) AGV’s status/error indicators around the time the front AGV moved out. Confirm whether the trailing AGV is faulted, or shows a fault coincident with being reported ready for a new task.
steps.purpose: Confirm the causal mechanism: the only time the front AGV can move without replacement is when the trailing AGV has a fault (including the case where it was ready and faulted at the same time).
steps.expected_result: You find live evidence that the trailing AGV had an active fault at (or coincident with) the time the front AGV moved out, consistent with the described pairing/backfill failure mechanism.
steps.healthy_condition: Trailing AGV shows no fault at the relevant time (or fault timing does not coincide with the front AGV move-out), suggesting the gap may be explained by other factors (e.g., chute fullness/exchange timing).
steps.failure_condition: Trailing AGV fault evidence is unclear or absent in RMS for the relevant time window.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you confirm trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing that would prevent proper backfill, stop further fault/backfill investigation and proceed to escalation guidance.

actions.label: Verify trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing
actions.exact_action: Check the trailing (behind) AGV status for a fault at the time the front AGV moved out; confirm whether the trailing AGV is faulted (or shows a fault coincident with being “ready for a new task”).

steps.title: If RMS is inconclusive, query WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) for trailing AGV fault/backfill failure evidence
steps.instruction: Using WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) (wcs_sql), query the OptiSweep DB for the same time window to find evidence of a fault/backfill failure for the trailing AGV (e.g., AGV state/error records).
steps.purpose: Provide database-backed evidence when RMS does not show a clear fault/backfill failure for the trailing AGV at the relevant time.
steps.expected_result: You identify live database evidence that the trailing AGV faulted (or otherwise failed to support backfill) during the exchange window corresponding to the front AGV move-out.
steps.healthy_condition: Database records show no fault/backfill failure for the trailing AGV in the relevant time window, shifting focus to chute fullness/closure and exchange timing.
steps.failure_condition: Database records do not show any trailing AGV fault/backfill failure evidence for the relevant time window.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you confirm trailing AGV fault/backfill failure evidence in the database, stop further chute/timing checks and proceed to escalation guidance.
If you do not find trailing AGV fault/backfill failure evidence, proceed to chute fullness/exchange timing checks.

actions.label: Query trailing AGV state/error records
actions.exact_action: If RMS shows no clear fault, use WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) (wcs_sql) to query the relevant OptiSweep DB tables/models for the same time window to find evidence of a fault/backfill failure for the trailing AGV (e.g., AGV state/error records).

steps.title: Check chute fullness/closure and exchange timing targets around the event
steps.instruction: Using WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) (wcs_sql), review live system data available for chute fullness and exchange timing metrics around the event time window. Look for conditions consistent with chute closure when the chute is full and exchange not completing before the 80% threshold (with exchange timing deviating from the median ~8 seconds and floor ~6.7 seconds).
steps.purpose: Validate the alternative contributing mechanism: chute closure is fullness-driven, and exchanges should complete before reaching 80% (median ~8s, floor ~6.7s).
steps.expected_result: You find live evidence that chute fullness/closure occurred (or was imminent) such that exchanges were not completed before the 80% threshold, and/or exchange timing deviated from the described targets (median ~8s, floor ~6.7s).
steps.healthy_condition: Chute fullness/closure did not occur before exchanges completed, and exchange timing aligns with the described targets (median ~8s, floor ~6.7s).
steps.failure_condition: Chute fullness/closure and exchange timing metrics do not align with the described mechanisms (i.e., no evidence of fullness-driven closure or timing deviation).
stop_or_escalate_if: If you confirm chute fullness/insufficient exchange rate consistent with chute closure before exchange completion, stop and escalate.
If chute fullness/exchange timing metrics do not align with the described mechanisms, escalate because the cause is not confirmed by the available evidence.

actions.label: Review chute fullness and exchange timing metrics
actions.exact_action: Check whether chute closure/fullness conditions could have occurred by reviewing live system data available via WCS/Helix DB (wcs_sql) for chute fullness / exchange timing metrics around the event; look for conditions consistent with “chute gets closed when the chute is full” and exchange not completing before the 80% threshold.

steps.title: Stop and escalate based on confirmed evidence (or lack of evidence)
steps.instruction: Based on your findings from RMS and WCS/Helix DB, decide whether to escalate. Escalate when you confirm the trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing mechanism or confirm chute fullness/insufficient exchange timing mechanism, or when you cannot confirm either mechanism with live evidence.
steps.purpose: Ensure the diagnostic outcome is actionable: either confirm the described mechanism with evidence or escalate when evidence is missing.
steps.expected_result: A clear diagnostic conclusion is produced: (1) trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing explains the missing backfill, and/or (2) chute fullness/closure and exchange timing targets indicate exchanges were not completed before 80%. If neither is supported by live evidence, escalation occurs due to unconfirmed cause.
steps.healthy_condition: Evidence supports one or both mechanisms described (trailing AGV fault timing and/or fullness-driven chute closure with exchange timing deviation).
steps.failure_condition: No live evidence supports trailing AGV fault/backfill failure and no live evidence supports chute fullness/closure or exchange timing deviation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if RMS and WCS/Helix DB do not show a trailing AGV fault/backfill failure and chute fullness/exchange timing metrics do not align with the described mechanisms.
Do not assume the cause solely from the event description; require live fault/state evidence for the trailing AGV and/or live chute fullness/exchange timing evidence.

actions.label: Escalate with evidence
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if you confirm the trailing AGV fault/ready+fault timing that would prevent proper backfill, or if you confirm chute fullness/insufficient tipping/exchange rate consistent with chute closure before exchange completion.

title: Check RMS / fleet status UI for AGVs waiting to exchange during shutdown or startup delay waiting on charger
summary: Use the RMS / fleet status UI to determine whether AGVs are not progressing due to state-transition failure visibility patterns: (1) AGVs waiting to do an exchange during shutdown, and/or (2) startup delay while waiting for an AGV on the charger. The system is described as exposing this via system faults and visible waiting conditions.
when_to_use: Use when lifecycle progression appears delayed during shutdown/startup and you need to check whether RMS is showing AGVs in the documented waiting/fault visibility patterns (exchange-waiting during shutdown; charger-waiting startup delay).

steps.title: Open RMS / fleet status UI and navigate to AGV status/errors overview
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) and navigate to the AGV status/errors overview area.
steps.purpose: Get to the live area where AGV waiting conditions and system faults/alerts are visible for diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: You are viewing the RMS AGV status/errors overview area where AGV waiting conditions and system fault/alert visibility can be checked.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS AGV status/errors overview area is populated and ready for inspection (not blank/unreachable).
steps.failure_condition: RMS is unreachable, the AGV status/errors overview area is blank, or you cannot view any fault/alert visibility needed for the diagnosis.
stop_or_escalate_if: RMS / fleet status UI cannot be accessed or the AGV status/errors overview area is not viewable.

actions.label: Open RMS fleet status UI
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) and navigate to the AGV status/errors overview area.

steps.title: Check for AGVs waiting to do an exchange during shutdown
steps.instruction: In the RMS AGV status/errors overview, look for AGVs showing a waiting condition consistent with “waiting to do an exchange” during shutdown.
steps.purpose: Identify the shutdown-related waiting condition described as visible in system faults/AGV waiting states.
steps.expected_result: At least one AGV is indicated in RMS as waiting to do an exchange during shutdown (or you determine none are indicated).
steps.healthy_condition: No widespread exchange-waiting indications are present when shutdown is expected to complete normally.
steps.failure_condition: You see one or more AGVs indicated as waiting to do an exchange during shutdown, especially if repeated/widespread.
stop_or_escalate_if: You observe repeated or widespread exchange-waiting indications that prevent lifecycle progression.

actions.label: Inspect exchange-waiting indications
actions.exact_action: Look for AGVs showing a waiting condition consistent with “waiting to do an exchange” during shutdown.

steps.title: Check for startup delay waiting for an AGV on the charger
steps.instruction: In the RMS AGV status/errors overview, look for startup delay evidence consistent with “waiting … for an AGV on the charger.”
steps.purpose: Identify the startup-related waiting condition described as visible in system faults/AGV waiting states.
steps.expected_result: At least one AGV is indicated in RMS as contributing to startup delay by waiting for an AGV on the charger (or you determine none are indicated).
steps.healthy_condition: No charger-waiting startup delay indications are present when startup proceeds normally.
steps.failure_condition: You see indications consistent with startup delay while waiting for an AGV on the charger, especially if repeated/widespread.
stop_or_escalate_if: You observe repeated or widespread charger-waiting indications that prevent lifecycle progression.

actions.label: Inspect charger-waiting indications
actions.exact_action: Look for startup delay evidence consistent with “waiting … for an AGV on the charger.”

steps.title: Confirm system faults/alerts align with the waiting conditions
steps.instruction: In the RMS AGV status/errors overview, confirm whether system faults/alerts are visible and align with the exchange-waiting and/or charger-waiting conditions you observed.
steps.purpose: Validate that RMS is reporting faults/alerts that correspond to the described waiting/failure visibility patterns.
steps.expected_result: RMS shows visible system fault/alert entries that align with the waiting conditions (or you determine there are no aligning fault/alert entries).
steps.healthy_condition: Fault/alert visibility is consistent with normal operation (no fault entries that match the described waiting patterns).
steps.failure_condition: Fault/alert visibility is present and aligns with exchange-waiting and/or charger-waiting indications, especially if repeated/widespread.
stop_or_escalate_if: You see repeated or widespread waiting/fault indications that prevent lifecycle progression.

actions.label: Inspect fault/alert visibility
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether the system is reporting faults/alerts that align with the above waiting conditions (system faults are explicitly mentioned as visible).

steps.title: Stop and escalate on repeated or widespread waiting/fault indications
steps.instruction: If you see repeated or widespread waiting/fault indications that prevent lifecycle progression (e.g., multiple AGVs stuck in exchange-waiting or charger-waiting states), stop and escalate for deeper investigation.
steps.purpose: Avoid spending time on further surface-level checks when the described failure visibility patterns are clearly preventing lifecycle progression.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated when the RMS evidence shows repeated/widespread waiting/fault indications consistent with the described patterns.
steps.healthy_condition: No repeated/widespread waiting/fault indications are present; lifecycle progression is not blocked by the described patterns.
steps.failure_condition: Repeated/widespread waiting/fault indications are present and escalation is not initiated.
stop_or_escalate_if: Multiple AGVs stuck in exchange-waiting during shutdown.
Multiple AGVs stuck in charger-waiting during startup delay.
System faults/alerts visible in RMS align with these waiting conditions and are repeated/widespread.

actions.label: Escalate

title: Disable/Enable a Charging Location From RMS Charger Selection to Manually Charge a Low-Power AGV

actions.label: Navigate to Charger Selection

actions.label: Check enabled/disabled status

steps.title: Disable the charger allocation (logical disable) for manual charging

steps.failure_condition: After clicking Disable, the charger status does not change to disabled.

steps.title: Physically push/position the low-power AGV into the disabled charging station

steps.expected_result: The low-power AGV is physically placed into the disabled charging station.

title: Check RMS disconnected AGV count and identify likely disconnect cause (lost RMS comms vs turned off)
summary: On the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary, read the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric. Use the training’s definition to interpret “disconnected” as AGVs that have lost communication from RMS (RMS runs on the server; AGVs are on Wi‑Fi), then correlate the disconnected count with likely causes: Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss vs AGVs being turned off.

not_for: Do not use this procedure as the only evidence to confirm a specific root cause when the disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether it is communication loss or AGVs being turned off (requires additional evidence beyond this metric).

steps.title: Open RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area

steps.healthy_condition: A single disconnected count value is displayed in the metric list.
steps.failure_condition: The disconnected count value is missing, inconsistent with the UI state, or cannot be read.

actions.label: Locate disconnected count
actions.exact_action: Locate and read the “disconnected” AGV count.

steps.purpose: Ensure the disconnected count is interpreted correctly before correlating causes.
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation of the disconnected count is explicitly tied to lost communication from RMS to AGVs over Wi‑Fi.
steps.healthy_condition: You can state that “disconnected” means lost communication from RMS to AGVs (RMS server application; AGVs on Wi‑Fi).
steps.failure_condition: You interpret “disconnected” as something unrelated to RMS communication loss (e.g., not tied to RMS/Wi‑Fi).

actions.label: Apply disconnected definition
actions.exact_action: Use the training definition: treat “disconnected” as AGVs that have lost communication from RMS (RMS is the application running on the server; AGVs are on the Wi‑Fi).

steps.expected_result: You produce a likely cause hypothesis that matches one of the two causes explicitly described: Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss or AGV turned off.
steps.healthy_condition: Your hypothesis aligns with the observed situation (e.g., if AGVs were turned off, you expect to see disconnect; if not, you consider Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot correlate the disconnected count to either communication loss with site Wi‑Fi or AGVs being turned off.
stop_or_escalate_if: Disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether the cause is communication loss vs AGVs being turned off (requires additional evidence beyond this metric).

actions.label: Correlate likely cause
actions.exact_action: Correlate the disconnected count with likely causes mentioned in the training: (1) AGV lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself, or (2) it was turned off.

steps.failure_condition: The overview screen does not appear after successful login.

title: Open RMS AGV fault drop-down to view current faults/errors
summary: Use the small drop-down in the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area to reveal current AGV fault/error items that need attention when the drop-down is hidden or collapsed.
when_to_use: When you need to view the current AGV faults/errors list from the RMS map monitor summary area and the drop-down is hidden/collapsed.

steps.title: Open the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) and navigate to the map monitor summary area that contains the Map Monitor Message Panel metrics and the small drop-down for AGV faults.
steps.purpose: Get to the RMS map monitor summary area where the AGV faults drop-down is located.
steps.expected_result: The RMS map monitor summary area is visible, including the small drop-down control associated with showing AGV faults.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the Map Monitor Message Panel metrics region that includes the AGV faults drop-down control.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS map monitor summary area is not visible or you cannot locate the AGV faults drop-down control in that region.

actions.label: Locate AGV faults drop-down region
actions.exact_action: Locate the small drop down here (AGV faults drop-down) in the RMS map monitor summary area.

steps.title: Expand the AGV faults drop-down if it is hidden/collapsed
steps.instruction: Check whether the AGV faults drop-down is visible. If it is hidden/collapsed, locate the drop-down control in the summary area and click it to expand.
steps.purpose: Reveal the current fault/error list items so they can be read.
steps.expected_result: The AGV faults drop-down expands and displays the current fault/error items list.
steps.healthy_condition: The drop-down expands from its collapsed/hidden state to show the errors list.
steps.failure_condition: The drop-down does not expand (remains hidden/collapsed) or no fault/error items appear when it is expanded.

actions.label: Click AGV faults drop-down
actions.exact_action: Click that drop down menu to see the errors.

steps.title: Read the current fault/error items from the expanded drop-down
steps.instruction: With the AGV faults drop-down expanded, read the list of current fault/error items shown in the drop-down.
steps.purpose: Identify which current AGV faults/errors are present from the RMS summary area.
steps.expected_result: The expanded drop-down shows a list of current fault/error items that need attention.
steps.healthy_condition: The drop-down contains one or more fault/error list items corresponding to current faults that need addressing.
steps.failure_condition: The drop-down shows no fault/error items even though other RMS indicators suggest active errors/warnings.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the drop-down does not reveal any faults while other indicators (e.g., message panel) show active errors/warnings.

actions.label: Read fault/error list
actions.exact_action: Read the errors shown in the expanded drop-down list.

steps.title: Stop and escalate when the drop-down list is insufficient for deeper investigation
steps.instruction: If the expanded drop-down shows faults that require deeper investigation and you cannot identify the affected AGV(s) or fault details from the drop-down list, stop and escalate.
steps.purpose: Avoid proceeding when the drop-down does not provide enough detail to identify affected AGV(s) or fault details.
steps.expected_result: You escalate rather than guessing when the drop-down list alone cannot identify the affected AGV(s) or provide sufficient fault details.
steps.healthy_condition: Fault/error items are identifiable enough from the drop-down list to determine what needs further investigation.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to proceed without being able to identify affected AGV(s) or fault details from the drop-down list.
stop_or_escalate_if: Drop-down shows faults requiring deeper investigation and affected AGV(s)/fault details cannot be identified from the drop-down list.

actions.label: Escalate for deeper investigation
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the drop-down shows faults that require deeper investigation and you cannot identify the affected AGV(s) or fault details from the drop-down list.

title: Review RMS open message panel for active errors/warnings and alarm history (past 24–48 hours)
summary: Use the RMS / fleet status UI open message panel to view pending messages containing active errors or warnings, and review the alarm history window covering roughly the past 24–48 hours.
when_to_use: When you need to quickly check whether the fleet has pending active error/warning messages and to review recent alarm history over the last ~24–48 hours.

steps.title: Open the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), navigate to the map monitor summary area where the open message panel is located.
steps.purpose: Get to the area where the open message panel and alarm history are available.
steps.expected_result: You are viewing the map monitor summary area that contains the open message panel.
steps.healthy_condition: The map monitor summary area is visible and the open message panel region is accessible/expandable.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate the open message panel region in the RMS / fleet status UI.

actions.label: Locate open message panel region
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS / fleet status UI / map monitor summary area).

steps.title: Expand/open the open message panel to view pending active errors/warnings

steps.healthy_condition: Pending messages are visible in the open message panel, and you can read the active error/warning entries from the panel contents.

actions.label: Open message panel
actions.exact_action: Find the “open message panel” area and open it to view pending messages that contain active errors or warnings.

steps.title: Review alarm history window in the same panel (past ~24–48 hours)
steps.instruction: Within the same open message panel view, review the alarm history list and confirm the displayed history window corresponds to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
steps.purpose: Confirm the alarm history time window and review recent alarm entries.
steps.expected_result: The alarm history list is visible and the time window shown corresponds to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
steps.healthy_condition: Alarm history entries are present for the expected recent window (about 24–48 hours).
steps.failure_condition: The alarm history window shown does not correspond to the past ~24–48 hours, or the alarm history cannot be reviewed due to missing/unclear window context.

actions.label: Check alarm history window
actions.exact_action: In the same panel, review the alarm history list and confirm the history window shown corresponds to the past ~24–48 hours.

steps.title: Stop and escalate when panel contents are insufficient to identify fault details
steps.instruction: If the open message panel indicates active errors/warnings requiring attention but you cannot identify the fault details from the panel contents, stop further interpretation and escalate.

title: Identify tote presence at sorter rack locations using RMS rack color (dark blue vs light blue)
summary: Use the RMS/map view rack location color to determine whether a sorter rack position is expected to have a tote present or is empty. Dark blue/violet indicates a tote is on the rack; light blue indicates the rack is empty. Use this to flag mismatches when a tote should exist at a sorter destination but the map shows the empty color.
when_to_use: When investigating a suspected tote addition/removal mismatch at a sorter destination and you need a quick, visual confirmation of tote presence/absence at specific rack locations in the RMS/map view.

steps.title: Open RMS/map view and locate the sorter destination rack locations
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS/map view), locate the sorter destination rack locations on the map for the rack position(s) you are investigating.
steps.purpose: Get to the live map view where rack locations are color-coded for tote presence/absence.
steps.expected_result: You can visually identify the specific rack position(s) on the RMS map for the sorter destination you are checking.
steps.healthy_condition: The sorter destination rack position(s) are visible on the RMS/map view and can be visually inspected for rack color.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the correct rack position(s) on the RMS map (wrong location/unclear rack selection), preventing a reliable color check.

actions.label: Open RMS/map view and find rack position
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS/map view) and locate the sorter destination rack locations on the map.

steps.title: Interpret rack color as tote present vs empty
steps.instruction: Visually check the rack location color for the specific rack position you are investigating and interpret it using the RMS color meaning: dark blue/violet = tote present; light blue = rack empty.
steps.purpose: Convert the RMS rack color into an observable tote presence/absence state.
steps.expected_result: For the rack position you are investigating, you determine one of two states based on color: dark blue/violet (tote present) or light blue (rack empty).
steps.healthy_condition: The rack color interpretation is unambiguous: dark blue/violet corresponds to tote present; light blue corresponds to empty.
steps.failure_condition: The rack color does not clearly match either tone (ambiguous/unclear display), or the color interpretation cannot be made reliably for the rack position.

actions.label: Check for dark blue/violet vs light blue
actions.exact_action: There are two distinct color... it's dark blue almost like a Violet... If a rack has this dark blue tone, it means it has a toad on it. If it has the light blue tone, it means it's empty.

steps.title: Compare observed rack color to expected tote presence at the destination
steps.instruction: Compare the observed rack color state (tote present vs empty) to what you expect to be present at that sorter destination (for example, you expect a tote there but the rack shows light blue).
steps.purpose: Determine whether the RMS map reflects the expected tote addition/removal state for the sorter destination.
steps.expected_result: You conclude whether the rack color matches expected tote presence or indicates a mismatch (expected tote but observed empty/light blue).
steps.healthy_condition: Observed rack color matches expectation (dark blue/violet when a tote is expected; light blue when no tote is expected).
steps.failure_condition: Observed rack color indicates empty (light blue) where a tote is expected, suggesting a tote addition/removal process problem.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the rack color indicates “empty” (light blue) where a tote should be present.

actions.label: Validate against expectation
actions.exact_action: Compare the observed rack color to what you expect to be present at that sorter destination (e.g., you expect to see a toad there, but maybe someone removed the wrong tote).

title: Determine Robot Status From Robot LED Colors (Purple/Blue/Green/Red) in Robot Selection Overview
summary: In the RMS / fleet status UI Robot Selection Overview, select a robot and use its two side LED color indications to determine whether it is disconnected, in task/searching for a label, idle, or in fault/low battery state.
when_to_use: Use when you need a first-pass determination of the selected robot’s state by reading the robot LED colors in the Robot Selection Overview.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the only diagnostic when the LED indicates fault/low battery; you must also check the message panel details for the specific fault/low battery information.

steps.title: Select the robot in the Robot Selection Overview
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI Robot Selection Overview, click/select the robot so its details are shown (the selected robot is highlighted with a box).
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct robot is selected so its LED indicators and details correspond to the robot you are assessing.
steps.expected_result: The selected robot is visibly highlighted (box around the selected robot) and its details panel is available.
steps.healthy_condition: A single intended robot is selected and highlighted in the Robot Selection Overview.
steps.failure_condition: No robot is highlighted/selected, or the highlighted robot is not the one you intend to assess.

actions.label: Select robot
actions.exact_action: click/select the robot so its details are shown

steps.title: Observe the robot’s two side LED colors
steps.instruction: Observe the robot’s two LEDs on each side in the Robot Selection Overview and note the LED color (purple, blue/flashing blue, green, or red).
steps.purpose: Read the robot’s LED indicators to determine its state.
steps.expected_result: You can identify the LED color state for the selected robot.
steps.healthy_condition: LED color is clearly one of: purple, blue/flashing blue, green, or red.
steps.failure_condition: LED color/state is unclear or does not match any of the documented colors/states.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the LED color does not match any documented color/state, stop and escalate for deeper RMS/WCS diagnostics (L2_support).

actions.label: Check LED colors
actions.exact_action: Observe the robot’s LED color indication (robots have two LEDs on each side)

steps.title: Map purple LED to “robot disconnected”
steps.instruction: If the LED is purple (often described as flashing purple), record the robot status as “robot disconnected.”
steps.purpose: Translate the observed LED color into the documented robot state.
steps.expected_result: Robot status is recorded as “robot disconnected” when the LED is purple/flashing purple.
steps.healthy_condition: Purple/flashing purple LED corresponds to “robot disconnected.”
steps.failure_condition: LED is purple but status is recorded as something else.

actions.label: Record status
actions.exact_action: Purple is robot disconnected

steps.title: Map blue/flashing blue LED to “robot in task/searching for label”
steps.instruction: If the LED is blue or flashing blue, record the robot status as “robot in task/searching for label” (flashing blue indicates the robot is looking for a label).
steps.purpose: Translate the observed LED color into the documented robot state.
steps.expected_result: Robot status is recorded as “robot in task/searching for label” when the LED is blue/flashing blue.
steps.healthy_condition: Blue/flashing blue LED corresponds to “robot in task/searching for label.”
steps.failure_condition: LED is blue/flashing blue but status is recorded as something else.

actions.label: Record status
actions.exact_action: Blue or flashing blue means robot is in task; flashing blue is robot is looking for a label

steps.title: Map green LED to “robot idle, not in a task”
steps.instruction: If the LED is green, record the robot status as “robot idle, not in a task.”
steps.purpose: Translate the observed LED color into the documented robot state.
steps.expected_result: Robot status is recorded as “robot idle, not in a task” when the LED is green.
steps.healthy_condition: Green LED corresponds to “robot idle/not in a task.”
steps.failure_condition: LED is green but status is recorded as something else.

actions.label: Record status
actions.exact_action: Green the robot is idle, not in task

steps.title: Map red LED to “robot has fault or low battery” and check message panel
steps.instruction: If the LED is red, record the robot status as “robot has fault or low battery,” and then check the message panel for the fault/low battery details.
steps.purpose: Identify fault/low battery state and corroborate details via the message panel.
steps.expected_result: Robot status is recorded as “robot has fault or low battery,” and the corresponding fault/low battery condition appears in the message panel.
steps.healthy_condition: Red LED corresponds to fault/low battery, and those conditions show up in the message panel.
steps.failure_condition: LED is red but no fault/low battery condition appears in the message panel, or the message panel does not provide actionable fault/low battery details.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the LED color/state does not match any documented colors/states, stop and escalate for deeper RMS/WCS diagnostics (L2_support).

actions.label: Record status
actions.exact_action: Red, the robot has fault or a low battery

title: Handle restart when robot cannot see a label: use indicator color states and verify map visibility after label reacquisition
summary: If a robot is restarted but does not snap back onto the map because it cannot see a label, use the documented indicator color behavior (flashing blue → solid blue; solid green indicates restart cycle/brakes locked) and perform the source-described physical label reacquisition steps. Then clear the E stop and confirm the robot appears successfully on the map.
when_to_use: Use when a robot was restarted but does not automatically snap back onto the map because it cannot see a label.

steps.title: Check whether the restarted robot snaps back onto the map
steps.instruction: On the RMS / fleet status UI map view, observe whether the restarted robot is displayed/positioned on the map.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the robot recovered automatically after restart or needs label reacquisition.
steps.expected_result: The robot is either displayed on the map (automatic recovery) or not displayed/positioned (needs further recovery steps).
steps.healthy_condition: After restart, the robot appears on the map.
steps.failure_condition: The robot does not snap back onto the map automatically after restart.

actions.label: Inspect map visibility for restarted robot
actions.exact_action: Check whether the robot snaps back onto the map automatically.

steps.title: If robot is not on the map, identify the flashing blue indicator state (cannot see a label)
steps.instruction: Locate the robot’s indicator and look for the documented “flashing blue sign” state indicating the robot can’t see a label.
steps.purpose: Confirm the documented cause for missing map visibility: the robot cannot see a label.
steps.expected_result: You observe the flashing blue indicator state when the robot cannot see a label.
steps.healthy_condition: Flashing blue corresponds to the robot searching/can’t see a label (as described).
steps.failure_condition: Indicator state does not match the expected flashing blue when the robot is missing from the map (requires escalation/SME guidance).

actions.label: Inspect robot indicator for flashing blue
actions.exact_action: Look for the documented indicator state described as a “flashing blue sign” indicating the robot can’t see a label.

steps.title: Perform physical label reacquisition: E stop the system and push the robot onto the label
steps.instruction: When the robot is in the flashing blue state, perform the physical recovery: E stop the system, walk into the floor, and push the robot onto the label.
steps.purpose: Force the robot to identify the label so it can lock on and recover map visibility.
steps.expected_result: After pushing the robot onto the label, the robot identifies the label and its indicator transitions from flashing blue to solid blue.
steps.healthy_condition: Robot is pushed onto the label location and begins label identification.
steps.failure_condition: Robot does not transition from flashing blue to solid blue after being pushed onto the label.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator does not transition from flashing blue to solid blue after pushing the robot onto the label, escalate.

actions.label: E stop the system (operator only)
actions.exact_action: E stop the system.

actions.label: Push robot onto the label
actions.exact_action: walk into the floor, push the robot onto the label.

steps.title: Verify indicator transition from flashing blue to solid blue after label pickup
steps.instruction: Observe the robot indicator and confirm it transitions from flashing blue to solid blue after it identifies the label.
steps.purpose: Confirm the robot has identified the label and is ready for E-stop clearing and map recovery.
steps.expected_result: Indicator goes from flashing blue to solid blue.
steps.healthy_condition: Flashing blue → solid blue transition occurs after label reacquisition.
steps.failure_condition: Indicator remains flashing blue or transitions to an unexpected state instead of solid blue.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator does not transition from flashing blue to solid blue after pushing the robot onto the label, escalate.

actions.label: Inspect indicator color transition
actions.exact_action: observe the documented indicator transition: it should go from flashing blue to solid blue.

steps.title: Clear E stop and verify the robot is successfully showing on the map
steps.instruction: Clear the E stop, then check the RMS / fleet status UI map view to confirm the robot is successfully showing on the map.
steps.purpose: Complete recovery by clearing E stop and confirming map visibility.
steps.expected_result: After clearing E stop, the robot appears successfully on the map.
steps.healthy_condition: Robot is displayed/positioned on the map after E-stop clear.
steps.failure_condition: Robot still does not appear on the map after clearing E stop.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the robot still does not appear on the map after clearing E stop, escalate.

actions.label: Clear E stop
actions.exact_action: clear the E stop.

actions.label: Verify robot on map
actions.exact_action: you'll see the robot being successfully showing successful on the map itself.

steps.title: If indicator is solid green, wait until it turns green before moving (brakes stay locked)
steps.instruction: If the robot is in the restart cycle state described as “solid green,” wait until it turns green before moving it because the brakes stay locked.
steps.purpose: Prevent unsafe movement while the robot’s brakes are described as locked during the restart cycle.
steps.expected_result: You do not move the robot while brakes are locked; you wait until the robot reaches the expected green state before moving.
steps.healthy_condition: Robot reaches the green state and you only move after it turns green.
steps.failure_condition: Moving the robot while brakes are described as locked (i.e., not in the expected green state).
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not attempt to move the robot while brakes are described as locked (e.g., when not in the expected green state).

actions.label: Inspect for solid green state
actions.exact_action: If the robot is in the restart cycle state described as “solid green,” wait until it turns green before moving it because brakes stay locked.

title: Verify Sorter Queue Routing: Entrance Queue → Queue Locations → Sorter Queue Locations → Exit Queue → Shutdown Queues
summary: Use the live sorter layout view (via RMS / fleet status UI when available, or site visual confirmation) to verify that AGVs/totes follow the documented sorter queue routing sequence: entrance queue first, then exchange staging (queue locations), then sorter queue locations for tote pickup/aisle entry, then exit queue after exchange, and finally shutdown queue positioning based on tote presence (including the 'off the end' path when entering shutdown from the entrance with a tote).
when_to_use: When you need to confirm that sorter queue routing is behaving correctly during normal sorter flow and during shutdown entry, specifically validating the expected queue-to-queue transitions and tote-dependent shutdown positioning.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a deep-dive into AGV charging behavior (charging-related issues are not the focus of this queue-routing check).

steps.title: Identify the sorter queue areas in the live layout view
steps.instruction: In the live sorter layout view available to support (RMS / fleet status UI when available), identify the following queue areas: entrance queue; queue locations (exchange staging); sorter queue locations (tote pickup / aisle entry); exit queue; shutdown queues (including under-rack shutdown locations for AGVs without totes and the shutdown location for AGVs with totes). If the live layout does not clearly label these areas, use site interview / visual confirmation to map the live labels to these documented queue-area names.
steps.purpose: Establish the exact queue-area names/locations to compare against observed AGV/tote routing.
steps.expected_result: You can point to (or otherwise map) each of the named queue areas in the live view: entrance queue, queue locations for exchange staging, sorter queue locations for tote pickup/aisle entry, exit queue, and shutdown queues with tote-dependent positioning.
steps.healthy_condition: All required queue areas are identifiable/mappable in the live view so you can track an AGV/tote through the full sequence.
steps.failure_condition: One or more queue areas cannot be mapped clearly in the live view, preventing reliable verification of routing transitions.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the live layout view does not clearly label these queue areas, stop and use the site interview/visual confirmation to map the live labels to the documented queue names.

actions.label: Map queue-area labels
actions.exact_action: Use site interview / visual confirm (to map live labels to entrance queue / exit queue / shutdown queue areas if needed)

steps.title: Confirm AGV/tote enters via the entrance queue first

steps.purpose: Validate the first routing constraint: anything entering the sorter area must go to the entrance queue first.
steps.expected_result: The observed AGV/tote appears first in the entrance queue (no bypass to later queue areas).
steps.healthy_condition: AGVs/totes entering the sorter area start in the entrance queue.
steps.failure_condition: An AGV/tote appears to bypass the entrance queue and appears directly in queue locations, sorter queue locations, exit queue, or shutdown queues.

actions.exact_action: After the entrance queue, confirm the AGV/tote transitions to the queue locations area where AGVs stage behind for an exchange

steps.failure_condition: The AGV/tote does not go to the exit queue after exchange.
